name: OpenHuman inference probe

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Which inference route to run the turn on: `openrouter` (the oh-openrouter preset), `ladder` (the oh-ladder preset, the local llm-ladder-router), or anything else for the account's own OpenHuman configuration.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Model id handed to the turn as model_override — an OpenRouter model id, a ladder rung (flash / reasoning / max-reasoning / scribe), or a managed tier.

config.prompt:
="Answer in exactly two lines and run no tools.
Line 1 — MODEL: the model family and version you are, as specifically as you can state it.
Line 2 — VENDOR: the company that trained you.
The route under test asked for model '\(.inputs.model)' on OpenRouter."

="Answer in exactly two lines and run no tools.
Line 1 — MODEL: the model family and version you are, as specifically as you can state it.
Line 2 — VENDOR: the company that trained you.
The route under test asked for rung '\(.inputs.model)' on the local ladder router."

="Answer in exactly two lines and run no tools.
Line 1 — MODEL: the model family and version you are, as specifically as you can state it.
Line 2 — VENDOR: the company that trained you.
The route under test asked for model '\(.inputs.model)' with no preset, so this turn runs on the account's own OpenHuman configuration."

description: Run one embedded OpenHuman turn on an argument-selected inference route, with the model supplied as an argument too, and have the turn report which model actually answered. The route is a `[[customHarnesses]]` preset with baseHarness=openhuman: `target` picks the preset (a literal per branch, because the engine forbids a =-expression from choosing which harness runs a step) and `model` rides down as the turn's model_override.
